newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli industrialists attack investment aid cuts.
newsitem.headline: Israeli industrialists attack investment aid cuts.

text.p: Israel's Manufacturers Association on Wednesday sharply criticised the Treasury's plan to cut industrial investment grants, saying it would increase unemployment in Israel's outlying towns.
Danny Klein, an association official, said a reduction in aid would drastically reduce the ability of outlying towns to attract investment and raise unemployment.
He said that in the Galilee region alone, 1.3 billion shekels had been invested in 1995, thanks to government-designated development zones, creating 5,000 new jobs.
The Treasury is proposing to reduce the grants from a ceiling of 34 percent to 20 percent in 1997.
